hole_addressed: WIN-014 c14 H2 (moderate): Our text states the Mohe dips are a '2.4–2.6σ excursion' (from raw-data values 6.0±2.5, 7.0±2.7 — accurate). But Wang et al. 2000's full text ALSO reports smoothed-curve values of 5.3 ± 1.4 and 6.8 ± 1.4 µGal (~3.8σ and ~4.9σ). A defender armed with the paper we link can quote the smoothed-curve significances back at us and claim selective quotation. Curmudgeon recommendation: 'Acknowledge and dispose in one clause: the higher smoothed-curve sigmas come from a 10-minute moving average that the paper itself concedes makes the signal looks more significant, and sigma computed on autocorrelated smoothed residuals is inflated; the raw-data 2.4-2.6 sigma is the honest figure. One sentence converts the omission into a demonstration of charity.'
analyst_assessment: Curmudgeon's c14 H2 reading is sound. Wang et al. 2000 published both a raw-data table (Table I) with the per-contact-phase amplitudes (6.0 ± 2.5 and 7.0 ± 2.7 µGal, giving the 2.4–2.6σ figure we already quote) and a 10-min moving-average analysis that returns the smaller-amplitude / smaller-uncertainty pair 5.3 ± 1.4 and 6.8 ± 1.4 µGal (~3.8σ and ~4.9σ). The moving-average operation is signal-shape-dependent (a coherent integration over a window of length τ raises SNR for any signal-component variation on timescales > τ) and the resulting residual time-series is autocorrelated by construction — adjacent samples in a sliding boxcar share τ−Δt of their integrand, so naive σ computed sample-by-sample understates true uncertainty by roughly √(Δt/τ_eff) where τ_eff is the effective decorrelation timescale (~the smoothing window). This is standard time-series statistics (Bartlett kernel HAC, Newey-West) and is the technically honest reason to prefer the raw-data σ when treating each sample as independent. A second, framing-level reason: WIN-014's argument is about the 2009 SG-network null, not the strength of the 1997 founding signal — κ is fixed by the dome at 10.9/6.5 = 1.677 nT/µGal regardless of whether the 1997 dip carries 2.5σ or 4.9σ confidence, and the 2009 prediction-vs-null refutation is independent of how confidently we believe the 1997 derivation data. Acknowledging the smoothed-curve numbers up front converts the appearance of selectivity into a demonstration of careful sourcing — exactly what the curmudgeon prescribes. The clause is single-paragraph, in-flow, and does not need a TLDR update because tldr_evidence does not currently quote any σ figure.
kernel_of_truth: Wang et al. 2000 measured a real instrument anomaly during the 1997 eclipse, and their smoothed-curve table shows the dip is robust to smoothing — a kernel of truth this clause should acknowledge. A defender is correct that smoothed-curve sigmas exceed raw-data sigmas; the question is which framing is statistically honest for the signal shape the dome model claims. For a sharp contact-phase pulse (the dome's own κ-coupled prediction shape), raw-data σ is the honest figure because the prediction is a delta-like spike; for a smooth aetheric build-up, smoothed σ would be appropriate. The dome's κ relation is dimensionally real (10.9 nT divided by 6.5 µGal gives 1.677 nT/µGal regardless of whether 6.5 is taken from raw or smoothed data, and the dome locks 1.677 by fiat). The failure point is downstream: applying that κ to 2009 gives a prediction the 2009 SG network did not record. The disposal clause respects the Wang 2000 measurement quality (instrument-class-honest, full-table cited) while showing WIN-014's argument is independent of which σ framing one prefers.

anticipated_objections: Objection: the smoothed-curve sigmas are not 'inflated' — they're the appropriate σ for the actual signal-extraction method Wang 2000 chose, and dismissing them as autocorrelation artifact is itself a selective reading. Response: the disposal clause acknowledges both numbers exist and explains which framing is honest for the dome's claimed signal shape (a contact-phase pulse — sharp, where raw-data σ is the honest figure; not a smooth aetheric build-up where smoothing would be appropriate). The disposal does not deny the smoothed values; it places them in a context where the WIN-014 argument is shown to be independent of σ framing.

Objection: by quoting the smoothed-curve values 5.3–6.8 µGal in the same paragraph as the predicted 3–9 µGal κ-pulse, we are inadvertently demonstrating that the Mohe 1997 founding signal MATCHES the κ prediction range — a defender will say 'see, your prediction worked once.' Response: the 1997 Mohe data is the κ-derivation data (the dome's own κ = 10.9/6.5 = 1.677 is computed FROM the 6.5 µGal Mohe excursion), so any agreement is by construction, not validation. The validation test is the 2009 SG network — which recorded a null. The disposal clause's final clause makes this explicit: 'the 2009 SG-network null falsifies the dome's own κ at face value regardless of how the 1997 founding dip is binned.'

Objection: the autocorrelation-inflation argument is a technical statistics claim that a non-specialist reader cannot evaluate, so the clause leans on credentialism the dome model has been criticized for elsewhere. Response: the clause provides a one-line plain-English explanation ('the moving average renders adjacent samples non-independent') that any reader who understands what a moving average does can verify mentally. The technical underpinning (Bartlett kernel HAC, Newey-West) is standard textbook time-series statistics and need not be cited; the plain-English version is sufficient for the rhetorical purpose of disposing the smoothed-σ defense.

Objection: adding more text to WIN-014 (already +47% from EXP-618 in cycle 13) is bloat. Response: the clause is two sentences, ~516 chars net. WIN-014 is the load-bearing China-SG-null finding and the most-attacked WIN in the kappa-cluster section, so disposing every defender argument here is high-value relative to length cost. The disposal clause replaces, in expected value, multiple curmudgeon cycles re-flagging the same hole.
